title: Import media and make a timeline
summary: Bring video clips into the project and put them on a new timeline.

steps.say: Click Edit on the bottom bar of the window to open the Edit page.

checks.prompt: Is the Edit page active, with the Edit icon highlighted on the bottom bar and a timeline across the lower part of the window?

hints: The page buttons are icons with labels in a row along the very bottom edge. Edit is one of them.
You can also press Shift 4 to jump straight to the Edit page.
steps.why: Every task in Resolve belongs to a page, and the Edit page has the tools for this lesson.

steps.say: Press Control I to open the import window.

checks.prompt: Is a file browser window open for choosing media to import?

hints: Hold the Control key and tap I, with the Resolve window in front.
You can also open the File menu at the top left, then choose Import, then Media.
steps.why: Importing adds your clips to the Media Pool without moving the files on disk.

steps.say: Choose one or more video clips, then click Open.

checks.prompt: Are there new clip thumbnails in the Media Pool at the top left that were not there before?

hints: Hold Control while clicking to pick several files at once, then press Enter.
If Resolve asks to change the project frame rate, choose Change to match your clips.
steps.why: You need clips in the Media Pool before you can edit them.

steps.say: Click one clip in the Media Pool, then press Control A to select them all.

checks.prompt: Are all the clips in the Media Pool highlighted as selected?

hints: The Media Pool is the panel at the top left with your clip thumbnails.
You can also drag a box around the thumbnails to select them.
steps.why: Selecting the clips first lets Resolve build the timeline from all of them at once.

steps.say: Right click a selected clip, point to Timelines, then choose Create New Timeline Using Selected Clips.

check.prompt: Is a New Timeline window open, or has a new timeline with clips appeared at the bottom?

hints: Right click directly on one of the highlighted thumbnails so the menu shows clip options.
Another way is to drag the selected clips down into the empty timeline area.
steps.why: A timeline is where you arrange clips into the order of your video.

steps.say: Type a name for the timeline, then click Create.

checks.prompt: Are clips now shown on the timeline tracks in the lower part of the window?

hints: The Timeline Name box is at the top of the New Timeline window.
If you skip the name, Resolve calls it Timeline 1, which is fine for now.
steps.why: Naming timelines helps when a project has several versions of an edit.

steps.say: Press Control S to save your project.
hints: If this is a new project, Resolve asks for a project name. Type one and click Save.
You can also use the File menu, then Save Project.
steps.why: Saving often protects your work if Resolve or the computer stops unexpectedly.
